title: The dual of a perfect complex
statement:
In the Poincare duality conventions of [def-pod-conventions] (an
instance of the setting of [def-sf-datum], with $X$ smooth,
separated of finite type and of pure dimension $d$), let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be perfect over $\Lambda_X$, at any
coefficient stage $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$.
The smooth dualizing-complex identification
$\eta_X:\omega_{X,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ of the
purity chapter (the orientation of [def-sf-orientation] for $f=a_X$)
and the twist interchange give a canonical isomorphism

$$
\mathbb D_XK\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K^\vee(d)[2d],
$$

natural in $K$, compatible with finite reduction, scalar extension,
shifts, and the canonical evaluation. Moreover $K^\vee$ is perfect, the
canonical map $K\to K^{\vee\vee}$ is an isomorphism, and consequently
$\mathbb D_X$ restricts to an anti-equivalence on the perfect objects,
the biduality $K\to\mathbb D_X\mathbb D_XK$ being, under this
identification, the coefficient-dual biduality $K\to K^{\vee\vee}$.

*Relative form.* The same holds for a smooth separated finite-type
$f:X\to Y$ of pure relative dimension $d$ over an arbitrary base $Y$ of the
setting: with the orientation $\gamma_f:\Lambda_X(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}
Rf^!\Lambda_Y$ of [def-sf-orientation] and
$\mathbb D_{X/Y}K=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,Rf^!\Lambda_Y)$, the composite of
$R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\gamma_f^{-1})$ with the twist interchange is a natural
isomorphism $\mathbb D_{X/Y}K\xrightarrow{\sim}K^\vee(d)[2d]$ for perfect
$K$, with the same biduality statement; the absolute case is $f=a_X$.

proof.text: Work first with the relative orientation already supplied in the statement. Write $\mathbf1=\Lambda_X$, $H(A,B)=R\mathcal Hom_X(A,B)$, $T=\Lambda_X(d)$, $L=T[2d]$, $W=Rf^!\Lambda_Y$, and $\lambda=\gamma_f^{-1}:W\xrightarrow{\sim}L$. Tensor products below are derived over the coefficient unit. The tensor--internal-Hom adjunction is part (i) of [sk-def-sf-operations]; its coefficient meanings are those of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], including the completed integral unit and the rational/common-stage operations. Thus $D_WK=H(K,W)$ and $K^\vee=H(K,\mathbf1)$. In the absolute case [def-pod-conventions] identifies $W=\omega_{X,\Lambda}$ and $\lambda=\eta_X$. We use the supplied orientation and its comparison maps from [def-sf-orientation]; we do not reconstruct purity or assume general Verdier biduality.

source.place: First arrow; relative and absolute notation

proof.text: Put $V=K^\vee=H(K,\mathbf1)$. The site's perfectness hypothesis is exactly the local finite-projective condition of [def-weil-site-perfect-complex], with its completed, localized and common-stage interpretations. By [prop-sf-dualizable], $V$ is site-perfect and the evaluation $e:K\otimes V\to\mathbf1$ is defined. The coefficient unit and its Tate twists are in the stated $D^b_{ctf}$ coefficient category: at finite level they are constructible locally free rank-one modules; at the integral stage they have the derived-complete lattice and finite free reductions of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and at the field stages they are its prescribed images. By [lem-sf-twist-interchange], $T$ is invertible locally constant of rank one, so the same applies to $L=T[2d]$. By [thm-sf-ctf-stability](ii),(vii), $V=H(K,\mathbf1)$ is in $D^b_{ctf}$ at all four stages. For every $M\in D^b_{ctf}$, [prop-sf-dualizable-hom] gives the isomorphism $a_M:V\otimes M\xrightarrow{\sim}H(K,M)$, namely the transpose of $e\otimes1_M$. We need it only for $M=K,\mathbf1,W,L$, all of which are in this domain: $W\cong L$ by the supplied orientation. In particular let $z:\mathbf1\to H(K,K)$ be the transpose of $1_K$ and define $c=a_K^{-1}z:\mathbf1\to V\otimes K$. Uncurrying $a_Kc=z$ gives $(e\otimes1_K)(1_K\otimes c)=1_K$, the first triangle. For the second set $r=(1_V\otimes e)(c\otimes1_V):V\to V$. The uncurrying of $a_{\mathbf1}r$ is $e(1_K\otimes r)=(e\otimes e)(1_K\otimes c\otimes1_V)=e$, using the first triangle; tensor bifunctoriality permits either evaluation to be applied first. This is also the uncurrying of $a_{\mathbf1}$. Injectivity of uncurrying and invertibility of $a_{\mathbf1}$ imply $r=1_V$. The uncurrying laws here are [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws]. We have constructed a global dual pair $(K,V,e,c)$ in each actual coefficient category from the canonical evaluation comparison, without inferring any equivalence from a definition or gluing local morphisms.

source.place: Expanded theorem proof, Step 5; perfect-duality unit prop-sf-dualizable and prop-sf-dualizable-hom, with coevaluation and both triangles derived from the canonical comparison at M=K

proof.text: Apply $H(K,-)$ to $\lambda$ and then [lem-sf-twist-interchange] with $m=d$ and $n=2d$ to obtain $\theta_{f,K}:H(K,W)\xrightarrow{H(K,\lambda)}H(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}K^\vee(d)[2d]$. The first arrow has inverse $H(K,\lambda^{-1})$ and the second is an isomorphism by that lemma since $K$ is perfect. Equivalently, under $K^\vee(d)[2d]=K^\vee\otimes L$, this composite is $(1_{K^\vee}\otimes\lambda)a_W^{-1}$: both versions of the twist comparison are inverse to the canonical evaluation comparison $a_L$ constructed in step 2. This proves exactly the prescribed composite, not merely the existence of an isomorphism.

source.place: First and second arrows, m=d and n=2d

proof.text: The evaluation compatibility is the typed equality $\lambda\,\mathrm{ev}_{K,W}=(\mathrm{ev}_{K,\mathbf1}\otimes1_L)(1_K\otimes\theta_{f,K})$ of maps $K\otimes H(K,W)\to L$; the right side uses associativity to put the last factor $L$ after $K\otimes K^\vee$. Indeed the defining uncurrying equation for $a_W$ is $\mathrm{ev}_{K,W}(1_K\otimes a_W)=e\otimes1_W$. Precompose the proposed equality with the isomorphism $1_K\otimes a_W$; both sides become $e\otimes\lambda$. The uncurrying equation and its functoriality are [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws]. For naturality, let $u:K\to K'$ and write $u^\vee=H(u,\mathbf1)$. Compare $\theta_{f,K}H(u,W)$ and $(u^\vee\otimes1_L)\theta_{f,K'}$, both from $H(K',W)$ to $K^\vee\otimes L$, by composing them with the isomorphism $a_L:K^\vee\otimes L\to H(K,L)$. Uncurrying these resulting maps gives, in both cases, $\lambda\,\mathrm{ev}_{K',W}(u\otimes1)$, by the displayed evaluation equation and naturality of evaluation. Injectivity of uncurrying and cancellation of $a_L$ prove the naturality square. The formula characterizes the comparison uniquely by evaluation.

source.place: Naturality of both arrows and identification of the actual evaluation

proof.text: For a finite-reduction or scalar-extension functor $F$, let $u:F\mathbf1\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1'$, $w:FW\xrightarrow{\sim}W'$, $l:FL\xrightarrow{\sim}L'$, and $h_{K,B}:FH(K,B)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(FK,FB)$ for $B=\mathbf1,W$ denote its prescribed comparisons; only these perfect-first-variable comparisons are used. [lem-fix-operation-reduction] supplies tensor and internal-Hom comparisons preserving evaluations, units, counits and associativity; between finite quotient rings its first-variable site-perfect hypothesis is satisfied by $K$. Its rationalization and common-stage clauses handle the two field stages with their prescribed, rather than discrete, coefficient operations. [def-sf-orientation] gives $\lambda' w=l F\lambda$. Define $v_K=H(FK,u)h_{K,\mathbf1}:F(K^\vee)\xrightarrow{\sim}(FK)^\vee$ and $r_K=H(FK,w)h_{K,W}:F(D_WK)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{W'}(FK)$. Under the tensor comparison the desired square is $\theta'_{f,FK}r_K=(v_K\otimes l)F(\theta_{f,K})$. Compose both sides with $a'_{L'}:(FK)^\vee\otimes L'\xrightarrow{\sim}H(FK,L')$ and uncurry. By preservation of evaluation, the left side is $\lambda'wF(\mathrm{ev}_{K,W})$ and the right side is $lF(\lambda)F(\mathrm{ev}_{K,W})$, with the prescribed tensor comparisons inserted. They agree by $\lambda'w=lF\lambda$; injectivity of uncurrying and cancellation of $a'_{L'}$ give the square. This proves the coefficient compatibilities, including their identity and tower compatibilities because each square is an equality for the prescribed comparisons.

source.place: Step 4, coefficient comparisons; returned step 5 up to its shift argument

proof.text: For shifts first work at finite or completed integral coefficients, with ordinary ringed-site internal Hom. At the integral stage [lem-sf-integral-line-tensor-comparison] identifies the prescribed completed tensor of the complete objects $\mathbf1$ and $V=H(K,\mathbf1)$ with the degree-zero line $T$ with their ordinary tensor, by the actual reduction-tower maps. Completeness here follows from their integral $D^b_{ctf}$ membership already checked in step 2. Apply [lem-sf-even-line-hom-shift] with $r=2d$ to the evaluation comparison $a_L$ and invert the resulting square. Naturality in the second variable of the signed shift isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] also commutes with $H(K,\lambda)$. Thus the composite $\theta_{f,K[s]}$ agrees with $\theta_{f,K}[-s]$ under the stated first-variable and tensor shift maps. The coefficient operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] give the rational images of this equality and its common finite-stage representative at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. This proves the shift clause for the actual canonical comparison, including its signs.

source.place: Step 4, shifts; replaces the signed Hom-complex and completed-tensor arguments of returned step 5

proof.text: The perfectness of $V=K^\vee$ is the conclusion of [prop-sf-dualizable] applied to $K$, and its $D^b_{ctf}$ membership was checked in step 2. Swap the dual pair of step 2 using the symmetry: its evaluation is $e'=e\sigma_{V,K}:V\otimes K\to\mathbf1$ and its coevaluation is $c'=\sigma_{V,K}c:\mathbf1\to K\otimes V$. Naturality and the hexagon law for the symmetry identify the two swapped triangle composites with the original ones: $(e'\otimes1_V)(1_V\otimes c')=(1_V\otimes e)(c\otimes1_V)=1_V$ and $(1_K\otimes e')(c'\otimes1_K)=(e\otimes1_K)(1_K\otimes c)=1_K$, with associators and unitors inserted. Thus both swapped triangles follow from the two explicit equations of step 2. Put $Z=H(V,\mathbf1)=K^{\vee\vee}$. Define $d:K\to Z$ to be the transpose of $e'$, so $d$ is precisely the canonical coefficient bidual map $\delta_K$. Define $t:Z\to K$ by $Z\xrightarrow{c'\otimes1_Z}K\otimes V\otimes Z\xrightarrow{1_K\otimes\mathrm{ev}_{V,\mathbf1}}K$. For $td$, replace $\mathrm{ev}_{V,\mathbf1}(1_V\otimes d)$ by $e'$; the result is the $K$ triangle, hence $td=1_K$. The uncurrying of $dt$ is $e'(1_V\otimes t)$; inserting the formula for $t$ and evaluating the first $V,K$ factors first reduces it, by the $V$ triangle, to $\mathrm{ev}_{V,\mathbf1}$. By [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws], $dt=1_Z$. Thus the actual canonical $\delta_K$ is an isomorphism. All these maps use the coefficient operations of step 1 and the global pair established by [prop-sf-dualizable-hom] in step 2; no claim that arbitrary dualizable objects are site-perfect is used.

source.place: Expanded theorem proof, Step 5; unit coefficient biduality, using the two triangles obtained from prop-sf-dualizable-hom

proof.text: By [prop-sf-dualizable], $V=K^\vee$ is site-perfect. Choose its local bounded finite-projective models from [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. By [lem-sf-twist-interchange], $T=\Lambda_X(d)$ is an invertible locally constant rank-one coefficient module. On a common refinement trivializing $T$, tensoring any model term with $T$ gives the same finite-projective term, since a direct-summand presentation of a finite sum of units is preserved under tensoring with a rank-one line. Tensoring the bounded complex and shifting by $[2d]$ therefore proves $V\otimes L$ site-perfect directly, at the integral stage using [lem-sf-integral-line-tensor-comparison] to identify ordinary tensor with completed tensor, and in the localized/common-stage presentations as well. In particular no dualizable-implies-site-perfect claim is required. Both $\mathbf1$ and $L$ belong to the stated coefficient category: at finite level a rank-one locally constant finite module is constructible and flat; at integral level its derived-complete lattice and finite free reductions are the ones specified in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and at the field stages take its prescribed images. Since $K\in D^b_{ctf}$, [thm-sf-ctf-stability](ii) for finite coefficients and (vii) for the integral and field stages give $V=H(K,\mathbf1)$ and $D_WK=H(K,W)$ in $D^b_{ctf}$, using $W\cong L$. Thus the isomorphism of step 3 proves that $D_WK$ is both site-perfect and in the required bounded constructible finite-Tor category.

source.place: Step 5, preservation of perfect objects; first paragraph of returned step 7

proof.text:
The negative-twist construction [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], with the invertibility assertion of [lem-sf-twist-interchange], gives the tensor inverse $L^{-1}=\Lambda_X(-d)[-2d]$ of $L$. Apply [lem-sf-invertible-hom-cancellation] to $V=K^\vee$ and $L$. It gives a specified isomorphism $i_K:H(V,\mathbf1)=K^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\sim}H(V\otimes L,L)$ whose transpose is
$$(V\otimes L)\otimes K^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{1_V\otimes\sigma_{L,K^{\vee\vee}}}V\otimes K^{\vee\vee}\otimes L\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}_{V,\mathbf1}\otimes1_L}L.$$
Put $\beta_K=H(\theta_{f,K}^{-1},\lambda):D_W^2K\xrightarrow{\sim}H(V\otimes L,L)$. Contravariance in the first variable gives the displayed source, and functoriality sends the two isomorphisms to an isomorphism. Thus $i_K^{-1}\beta_K$ is precisely the evaluation-defined inverse-twist cancellation after applying the orientation/twist comparison twice.

source.place: Step 5, inverse-twist cancellation; replaces the explicit line-pair inverse in returned step 7

proof.text:
Define the canonical $W$-biduality $\delta_{W,K}:K\to D_W^2K$ as the transpose of $\mathrm{ev}_{K,W}\sigma_{D_WK,K}$. By the evaluation equality in step 4, uncurrying $\beta_K\delta_{W,K}$ gives
$$(V\otimes L)\otimes K\xrightarrow{1_V\otimes\sigma_{L,K}}V\otimes K\otimes L\xrightarrow{(e\sigma_{V,K})\otimes1_L}L.$$
Uncurrying $i_K\delta_K$ gives the same map: the defining equation for coefficient biduality from step 7 is $\mathrm{ev}_{V,\mathbf1}(1_V\otimes\delta_K)=e\sigma_{V,K}$. Hence $\beta_K\delta_{W,K}=i_K\delta_K$ by injectivity of uncurrying [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws]. Consequently $i_K^{-1}\beta_K$ identifies the actual $W$-biduality with the coefficient biduality, which step 7 proves invertible. All displayed symmetries are the derived ones. In particular the even line shift contributes $(-1)^{2dr}=1$ when moved past degree $r$; no unsigned double-dual identification is substituted.

source.place: Step 5, identification of the actual bidual morphism; final calculation of returned step 7

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P$ be the full category of site-perfect objects in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. Step 8 has separately checked site-perfectness and $D^b_{ctf}$ membership of $D_WK$ using [def-weil-site-perfect-complex] and [thm-sf-ctf-stability](ii),(vii). Thus internal Hom defines $F=D_W:\mathcal P^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal P$. Its opposite is $G:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P^{\mathrm{op}}$. The biduality maps are natural: for $u:A\to B$, both $D_W^2(u)\delta_{W,A}$ and $\delta_{W,B}u$ transpose to evaluation with $u$ in its $A$ input, by naturality of evaluation and [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws]. Step 10 proves these natural maps invertible, hence $FG\cong\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal P}$; taking opposites gives $GF\cong\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal P^{\mathrm{op}}}$. These are the equivalence data. Setting $f=a_X$, $W=\omega_{X,\Lambda}$ and $\lambda=\eta_X$ gives every absolute clause by [def-pod-conventions]. The proof works over every base in the setting with the supplied relative orientation.

proof_origin.place: Retained current-blueprint route and returned proof; extracted integral-line tensor comparison, signed even-line shift square, and invertible internal-Hom cancellation into statement-only lemmas; retained other proof steps verbatim.

and the twist interchange give a canonical isomorphism

$$

natural in $K$, compatible with finite reduction, scalar extension,

canonical map $K\to K^{\vee\vee}$ is an isomorphism, and consequently
$\mathbb D_X$ restricts to an anti-equivalence on the perfect objects,
the biduality $K\to\mathbb D_X\mathbb D_XK$ being, under this

*Relative form.* The same holds for a smooth separated finite-type
$f:X\to Y$ of pure relative dimension $d$ over an arbitrary base $Y$ of the
setting: with the orientation $\gamma_f:\Lambda_X(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}
Rf^!\Lambda_Y$ of [def-sf-orientation] and
$\mathbb D_{X/Y}K=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,Rf^!\Lambda_Y)$, the composite of
$R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\gamma_f^{-1})$ with the twist interchange is a natural
isomorphism $\mathbb D_{X/Y}K\xrightarrow{\sim}K^\vee(d)[2d]$ for perfect
$K$, with the same biduality statement; the absolute case is $f=a_X$.

proof.text:
Step 1: the definition. By [def-pod-conventions],
$\mathbb D_XK=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\omega_{X,\Lambda})$ with
$\omega_{X,\Lambda}=Ra_X^!\Lambda$, and
$K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$.

Step 2: the smooth purity input. The smooth dualizing-complex
identification of [cor-pur-finite-stage-smooth-dualizing-complex]
(at the finite stage $A=A_{E,n}$) and its transport
[cor-pur-adic-and-rational-smooth-dualizing-complexes] (at the
$\mathcal O_E$-, $E$- and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-stages) provide the
canonical orientation

$$
\eta_X:\omega_{X,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_X(d)[2d],
$$

which is the case $f=a_X$ of an orientation datum as in
[def-sf-orientation], compatible with finite reduction, scalar
extension, and shifts.

Step 3: substitution and interchange. Substituting $\eta_X$ into the
internal Hom and using the shift of the second variable,

$$
\mathbb D_XK\cong R\mathcal Hom_X\bigl(K,\Lambda_X(d)[2d]\bigr)
\cong\bigl(R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X(d))\bigr)[2d]
\cong K^\vee(d)[2d],
$$

the second isomorphism being the shift axiom of the derived internal Hom
of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the third being
[lem-sf-twist-interchange] with $m=d$ (its hypothesis is the
perfectness of $K$ over $\Lambda_X$).

Step 4: canonicality and compatibilities. The composite is canonical
because its ingredients are: the orientation is the canonical one of the
purity chapter, and the twist interchange and the shift identification
are canonical maps of the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction (natural in
$K$; on the generators $K=\Lambda_X^r$ they are the coordinate
isomorphisms; the shift index is the constant $2d$). Naturality in $K$
and compatibility with finite reduction, scalar extension and shifts
follow from the corresponding properties of $\eta_X$ recorded in
[cor-pur-finite-stage-smooth-dualizing-complex] and
[cor-pur-adic-and-rational-smooth-dualizing-complexes], and of the
derived tensor and internal Hom recorded in
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The compatibility with the
canonical evaluation is the compatibility of the twist interchange with
the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]: the evaluation is the counit,
and the interchange carries the counit for $K\otimes^L\Lambda_X(d)$ to
the counit for $K$ tensored with the identity of $\Lambda_X(d)$, after
unwinding $K^\vee(d)\otimes\Lambda_X(d)$ through the associativity and
commutativity coherence of the derived tensor product.

Step 5: biduality and the anti-equivalence. By [prop-sf-dualizable],
$K^\vee$ is perfect and the evaluation $K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}K^\vee\to\Lambda_X$
is defined. Choose locally a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finite
projective $\Lambda_X$-modules with a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to K$.
By [prop-sf-dualizable-hom] (with $M=\Lambda_X$) the dual $K^\vee$ is
represented by $P^{\bullet\vee}$, again bounded with finite projective
terms, and applying this once more $K^{\vee\vee}$ is represented by
$P^{\bullet\vee\vee}$; the canonical map $K\to K^{\vee\vee}$ is then
termwise the double-dual map $P^j\to P^{j\vee\vee}$, an isomorphism by
[lem-sf-hom-finite-projective], compatible with the differentials,
so $K\to K^{\vee\vee}$ is an isomorphism (the statement being local on
the site). Applying Step 3 twice,
$\mathbb D_X\mathbb D_XK\cong\bigl(K^\vee(d)[2d]\bigr)^\vee(d)[2d]\cong K^{\vee\vee}$,
where $\bigl(K^\vee(d)[2d]\bigr)^\vee\cong R\mathcal Hom_X(K^\vee,\Lambda_X(-d)[-2d])\cong K^{\vee\vee}(-d)[-2d]$
by the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] (moving the invertible twist
